description:
The six public functions exported under the oscal feature take or return serde_json::Value directly:

  pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs:99    pub fn assessment_results(report: &EvaluationReport) -> Value
  pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs:442   pub fn risks_from_store(store: &DeviationStore) -> Vec<Value>
  pkix-lint/src/oscal/parse.rs:547  pub fn deviation_store_from_risks(value: &Value) -> Result<DeviationStore, ParseError>
  pkix-lint/src/oscal/parse.rs:889  pub fn lint_ids_from_catalog(value: &Value) -> Result<Vec<String>, ParseError>
  pkix-lint/src/oscal/catalog.rs:101 pub fn catalog_from_lints(lints, catalog_id, catalog_version) -> Value
  pkix-lint/src/oscal/profile.rs:203 pub fn resolve_profile(profile: &Value, sources: &HashMap<String, Value>) -> Result<ResolvedProfile, ParseError>

This pins serde_json's major version (currently 1.x, stable for years but not zero-risk) into pkix-lint's public oscal-feature API. A hypothetical serde_json 2.0 forces every pkix-lint consumer using the oscal feature to coordinate the upgrade. The coupling is gratuitous — pkix-lint does not expose a JSON-DOM-shaped API for any reason intrinsic to its model.

CALLER IMPACT:

Today, a caller writing:
  let assessment = pkix_lint::oscal::emit::assessment_results(&report);
  serde_json::to_string_pretty(&assessment)?

depends on `assessment: serde_json::Value`. If pkix-lint and the caller end up with different serde_json majors due to MSRV, dep-tree resolution, or a transitive bump, the type stops unifying and compilation breaks.

A caller wanting to use jiff_json (hypothetical) or sonic_rs as their JSON layer cannot — they must serialize the pkix-lint Value first and reparse, which defeats the point.

ARCHITECTURAL ANGLE: Per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6, pkix-lint's public surface must "remain possible to cache" and "be Send+Sync." serde_json::Value satisfies both today, but the wider problem — pkix-lint's API stability depends on a third-party crate's API stability — is exactly what the framework-not-policy non-negotiable #5 wants to avoid.

REMEDIATION OPTIONS:

1. Return String / &str / Vec<u8> from emit functions; accept &str / &[u8] in parse functions. Internal serde_json work happens entirely inside pkix-lint. Callers depend on whatever JSON layer they want.
   - Slight perf cost on the emit side (re-serialize) but the OSCAL output is already serialized for almost every caller use case (writing to disk, transmitting, etc.).
   - Standard pattern for crates that want to control their own dependency surface.

2. Wrap serde_json::Value in opaque newtypes:
   pub struct OscalAssessmentResults(serde_json::Value);
   pub struct OscalCatalog(serde_json::Value);
   pub struct OscalProfile(serde_json::Value);
   pub struct OscalRisks(serde_json::Value);
   with .as_value() / .to_string() / .from_str() methods. Callers pass these around; pkix-lint absorbs any serde_json major bump internally by changing only the .as_value() method.
   - Preserves the zero-copy "build JSON DOM then serialize once" pattern.
   - Pre-1.0 free if added now.

3. Document the serde_json major-version pin commitment explicitly and accept it. This is the cheapest option but ties pkix-lint to serde_json forever — a real cost the maintainer should make deliberately, not by default.

Option 2 (opaque newtype) is the highest-flexibility / lowest-friction choice. It costs ~30 lines per type and produces no caller-visible behavioral change.

CASCADE: This finding is structurally identical to PKIX-7f92.7 (rfc_section_id/rfc_url) but at the module-API scale rather than the trait-method scale. Same fix pattern (typed wrapper, deprecation alias if needed).
title: serde_json::Value leaks through 6 public OSCAL APIs (assessment_results, risks_from_store, deviation_store_from_risks, lint_ids_from_catalog, catalog_from_lints, resolve_profile); serde_json major-version pinned into pkix-lint public surface
